study_identification_part.si4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly state the aims to quantify neuroanatomical heterogeneity in CHR-P versus healthy controls and relative to transition status, using VR/CV and PBSI normative analyses. This directly presents research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed to quantify the neuroanatomical heterogeneity ... in CHR-P individuals compared with healthy controls (HC), and in relation to subsequent transition... Regional heterogeneity was indexed with the Variability Ratio (VR)... Personalised estimates ... using a normative modelling approach, to assess the ' normativeness ' of neuroanatomical profiles in individuals at CHR-P.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort (HC) comes from the ENIGMA CHR-P dataset; basic description and ethics/consent are provided and QC exclusions are outlined (outliers ±2 SD, >5% missing ROIs removed). However, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria for healthy controls are deferred to prior work and not fully described here.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The ENIGMA CHR-P dataset amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 sites, comprising 1579 individuals... and 1243 HC participants... Further participant inclusion and exclusion criteria have been previously described [20]... The ENIGMA quality control procedure identifies outliers (±2 SD from the mean) and includes a visual inspection... Participants with >5% missing ROIs were excluded from the current analyses.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age, sex, and site/scanner effects were explicitly modeled; neuroimaging data were harmonized with neuroComBat controlling for group, age, and sex to address site effects, and regressions adjusted for age and sex.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: Neuroimaging data were adjusted for scanner protocol and site using neuroComBat... while controlling for group (CHR-P/HC), age and sex... All multivariable regression models were applied, adjusting for age and sex.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study clearly states the reference data are drawn from the multi-site ENIGMA CHR-P dataset covering 29 international sites, identifying it as the source of neuroimaging data.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The ENIGMA CHR-P dataset amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 sites... comprising 1579 individuals... and 1243 HC participants.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Imaging data were secondary, pooled from existing ENIGMA CHR-P sites; per guidance, acquisition protocol details for secondary data are not required for this item.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps and software are described: FreeSurfer automated pipelines following the ENIGMA protocol with specific steps (motion correction, Talairach transform, skull stripping, segmentation, normalization), QC via outlier detection and visual inspection, exclusion for >5% missing ROIs, and neuroComBat harmonization.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: All neuroimaging data were processed according to FreeSurfer automated pipelines... includes motion correction, automated Talairach transformation, skull stripping, segmentation... intensity normalisation. The ENIGMA quality control procedure identifies outliers (±2 SD)... visual inspection... Participants with >5% missing ROIs were excluded... Neuroimaging data were adjusted for scanner protocol and site using neuroComBat...

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The analyses used the full dataset without train/test partitioning or cross-validation for the normative PBSI or VR/CV modeling; no internal hold-out or resampling scheme for model validation is reported.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: This calculation was conducted across each ROI to compare baseline variability... We applied the log-VR... PBSI... calculated... Group-level comparisons... No mention of data splits or cross-validation.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: All analyses were performed within the ENIGMA CHR-P dataset; the paper does not apply the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The ENIGMA CHR-P dataset amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 sites... analyses... conducted within R... Group-level comparisons... (no external dataset described).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is detailed: VR/CV formulas implemented with metafor/meta in R 4.0.3, and the PBSI normative method is explained including correlation-based computation, normative reference to HC, and z-score thresholding.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: All analyses were conducted within R v .4.0.3; the VR analyses were conducted using the metafor and meta packages... Variability ratio... calculated... Person-Based Similarity Index... concatenating regional measures... correlated with the corresponding profiles of the members of the HC group... transformed into z-scores... threshold >1.5 SD.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Although heterogeneity statistics (VR/CV and PBSI outcomes) are reported, there are no quantitative model performance metrics assessing fit or calibration of a normative model (e.g., prediction error or coverage); the results focus on group comparisons and deviation counts.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Regional SA... trend towards greater variability... did not survive FDR... Within-group PBSI... greater within-group variability... Normative PBSI... counts of marked deviation... (no metrics of model fit/calibration).

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning (train/validation/test) was performed; analyses used the full dataset, so characteristics per partition are not applicable.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software versions are provided (R 4.0.3; FreeSurfer versions listed per site) and code availability is stated upon request, but there is no publicly accessible code or data link, limiting reproducibility.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: All analyses were conducted within R v .4.0.3... Freesurfer version [site table]... Computer code to calculate the VR, CVR and PBSI statistics is available from the authors upon request.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses examined clinical moderators such as transition status, subgroup status (APS/BLIPS/GRD), antipsychotic exposure, and baseline psychopathology (CAARMS/SIPS z-scores) with multivariable models adjusting for age and sex.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: In both PBSI analyses, we also investigated the potentially moderating effects of transition status (CHR-T/CHR-NT), subgroup status (APS/BLIPS/ GRD), antipsychotic exposure, and overall baseline psychopathology (total CAARMS/SIPS severity z-scores)... All multivariable regression models were applied, adjusting for age and sex.
